articles.title: उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी की लहर समाप्त हो गई है, जबकि मध्य वियतनाम में यह 18 अगस्त तक जारी रहेगी। - Vietnam.vn

articles.full_text:
14 अगस्त की दोपहर को, राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र ने बताया कि उत्तरी क्षेत्र, थान्ह होआ और न्घे आन में बारिश हुई, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हुई।
उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी की लहर समाप्त हो गई है, जबकि मध्य वियतनाम में यह 18 अगस्त तक जारी रहेगी।
कई दिनों की भीषण गर्मी के बाद उत्तरी क्षेत्र में बारिश हुई, जिससे 14 अगस्त से चल रही लू का अंत हो गया। वहीं, मध्य क्षेत्र में लू जारी है, जहां कुछ इलाकों में तापमान 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो गया है, और पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार यह 18 अगस्त तक जारी रहेगी।
मौसम विभाग ने बताया है कि अगले दो दिनों में उत्तर में लू का प्रकोप समाप्त हो जाएगा। आज शाम और रात भर उत्तर, थान्ह होआ, न्घे आन, हा तिन्ह , मध्य उच्चभूमि और दक्षिण में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें जारी रहेंगी। आमतौर पर 10-30 मिमी बारिश होगी, जबकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में 80 मिमी से अधिक बारिश हो सकती है।
इस बीच, मध्य वियतनाम में लू का प्रकोप जारी है। 15 अगस्त को, क्वांग त्रि से दा नांग शहर तक का क्षेत्र, क्वांग न्गाई से डाक लक और खान्ह होआ प्रांतों के पूर्वी हिस्से में भीषण गर्मी बनी रही, कुछ क्षेत्रों में तो अत्यधिक गर्मी का प्रकोप देखा गया। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा, जबकि कुछ स्थानों पर यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक था।
16 अगस्त को, भीषण गर्मी की लहर मध्य वियतनाम में उत्तर की ओर फैल गई, जिससे न्घे आन से दा नांग शहर तक का क्षेत्र, क्वांग न्गई से डाक लक तक के प्रांतों के पूर्वी भाग और खान्ह होआ प्रभावित हुए। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा, जबकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक था।
मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान एजेंसी के अनुसार, उपर्युक्त क्षेत्रों में फैली भीषण गर्मी की लहर 18 अगस्त तक जारी रहने की संभावना है।
शाम 4:50 बजे, दक्षिणी वियतनाम मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान केंद्र ने बताया कि मौसम रडार से प्राप्त तस्वीरों में हो ची मिन्ह शहर के उत्तरी भाग में घने तूफानी बादलों का निर्माण होता दिख रहा है। अगले एक घंटे के भीतर, ये तूफानी बादल दक्षिण-पश्चिम से उत्तर-पूर्व दिशा में आगे बढ़ेंगे और हो ची मिन्ह शहर क्षेत्र से निकल जाएंगे।
हालांकि, हो ची मिन्ह शहर के दक्षिण-पश्चिम में स्थित ताई निन्ह क्षेत्र में गरज-चमक वाले बादल दक्षिण की ओर बढ़ रहे हैं और इनके कारण गरज-चमक जारी रहेगी। इस क्षेत्र के निवासियों को व्यस्त समय में यात्रा करते समय गरज-चमक से बचाव के लिए सावधानी बरतनी चाहिए।
हो ची मिन्ह सिटी के अन्य क्षेत्रों में फिलहाल कम बारिश होगी। हालांकि, आंधी-तूफान अचानक आ सकते हैं, इसलिए लोगों को मौसम के घटनाक्रम पर नजर रखनी चाहिए, खासकर बाहर यात्रा करते समय।

articles.title: हनोई में स्थानीय स्तर पर भीषण गर्मी की लहर जारी है। - Vietnam.vn

articles.full_text:
उत्तरी वियतनाम मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान केंद्र द्वारा दोपहर 2 बजे जारी बुलेटिन के अनुसार, हनोई के कई कम्यूनों और वार्डों में आज दोपहर 1 बजे तापमान कुछ दिनों पहले की तुलना में काफी गिर गया है।
हनोई में स्थानीय स्तर पर भीषण गर्मी की लहर जारी है।
14 अगस्त की दोपहर को हनोई में आंधी-तूफान आया, जिससे तापमान में गिरावट आई। अगले तीन दिनों तक शहर में केवल कुछ इलाकों में ही भीषण गर्मी पड़ने की संभावना है।
विभिन्न स्थानों पर तापमान का माप इस प्रकार है: सोन ताय 25.0°C; बा वी 24.9°C; लैंग 25.5°C; हा डोंग 25.0°C; होआई डुक 24.7°C... सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 89 - 92% के बीच रहती है।
पूर्वानुमानों के अनुसार, लगभग 22-25 डिग्री उत्तरी अक्षांश पर स्थित निम्न दबाव क्षेत्र के प्रभाव से उत्तरी क्षेत्र में अपसारी पवन क्षेत्र कमजोर हो जाएगा। कल (15 अगस्त) और 16 अगस्त को हनोई में धूप खिली रहेगी और कुछ स्थानों पर लू भी चलेगी। अधिकतम तापमान 34-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा।
मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान एजेंसी के 14 अगस्त की दोपहर के मौसम पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, 17 अगस्त को भी शहर में छिटपुट लू चलने की संभावना है, साथ ही शाम को बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की भी संभावना है। लू के कारण प्राकृतिक आपदा का खतरा स्तर 1 है।
तीव्र गर्मी और कम आर्द्रता के प्रभाव के कारण, बिजली की बढ़ती मांग के चलते आवासीय क्षेत्रों में आग और विस्फोट का खतरा है, साथ ही जंगल में आग लगने का खतरा भी बढ़ गया है।
इसके अलावा, आने वाले दिनों में हनोई में गर्म मौसम के कारण लंबे समय तक उच्च तापमान के संपर्क में रहने वाले लोगों में निर्जलीकरण, थकावट और लू लगने जैसी समस्याएं हो सकती हैं।
मौसम विज्ञान एजेंसी ने यह भी बताया कि लू की चेतावनी में तापमान का पूर्वानुमान और बाहर का वास्तविक तापमान 2-4 डिग्री सेल्सियस या उससे भी अधिक भिन्न हो सकता है, जो कंक्रीट या डामर जैसी सतह की स्थितियों पर निर्भर करता है।

articles.title: अल नीनो से बढ़ा समुद्र का जलस्तर, 2026 में फिर बढ़ी चिंता: शोध - Down to Earth- Hindi
articles.search_term: ("पारा चढ़ा" OR "पारा पहुंचा" OR तापमान OR "तापमान बढ़ा" OR "रिकॉर्ड तोड़ गर्मी" OR "डिग्री सेल्सियस" OR "पारा उबला" OR "अधिकतम तापमान" OR "तापमान 40 पार" OR "तापमान 45 पार" OR "तापमान बढ़ने की संभावना") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
अल नीनो के दौरान वैश्विक समुद्री जलस्तर बढ़ा, जिसमें जमीन से समुद्र में पहुंचे पानी की भूमिका सबसे ज्यादा रही।
2023-24 के अल नीनो में समुद्री जलस्तर तेजी से बढ़ा, जबकि हिंद महासागर और सकारात्मक आईओडी का असर भी दिखा।
दक्षिण अमेरिका में कम बारिश से जमीन का पानी घटा और अधिक पानी समुद्र में पहुंचा, जिससे जलस्तर बढ़ा।
2014-16 और 2023-24 के अल नीनो में समुद्री जलस्तर बढ़ा, लेकिन क्षेत्रीय बारिश और जलवायु परिस्थितियां अलग रहीं।
2026 में मजबूत अल नीनो की आशंका से वैश्विक तापमान बढ़ने और समुद्र के जलस्तर में तेज वृद्धि का खतरा है।
अल नीनो और ला नीना दुनिया के मौसम और जलवायु को प्रभावित करने वाली बड़ी प्राकृतिक घटनाएं हैं। अल नीनो के दौरान प्रशांत महासागर के भूमध्यरेखीय हिस्से का पानी सामान्य से अधिक गर्म हो जाता है। इसके उलट ला नीना में यह पानी सामान्य से अधिक ठंडा होता है। इन घटनाओं का असर केवल समुद्र के तापमान तक सीमित नहीं रहता, बल्कि दुनिया के तापमान, बारिश और समुद्र के बढ़ते जलस्तर पर भी पड़ता है।
जर्नल ऑफ जियोफिजिकल रिसर्च: ओशन्स पत्रिका में प्रकाशित एक नए अध्ययन में 2014-16 और 2023-24 के दो मजबूत अल नीनो घटनाक्रमों की तुलना की गई है। शोधकर्ताओं ने पाया कि दोनों घटनाओं के दौरान दुनिया के औसत समुद्री जलस्तर में बढ़ोतरी हुई। हालांकि दोनों बार इसके पीछे कारणों और अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों के योगदान में काफी अंतर था।
2023-24 में समुद्र का जलस्तर तेजी से बढ़ा
शोध के अनुसार, 2014-16 के अल नीनो के विकास के दौरान दुनिया का औसत समुद्री जलस्तर करीब 9.16 मिमी बढ़ा। वहीं, 2023-24 के अल नीनो के दौरान यह बढ़ोतरी करीब 7.70 मिमी रही।
पहली नजर में 9.16 मिलीमीटर की बढ़ोतरी ज्यादा लगती है, लेकिन 2023-24 की घटना कम समय में हुई। इसलिए उस दौरान समुद्र के जलस्तर बढ़ने की गति काफी तेज थी। वैज्ञानिकों के लिए यह बात खास महत्व रखती है, क्योंकि समुद्र का जलस्तर तेजी से बढ़ने पर तटीय इलाकों पर दबाव भी तेजी से बढ़ सकता है।
जमीन से पानी समुद्र में पहुंचा
समुद्र का जलस्तर बढ़ने के दो प्रमुख कारण होते हैं। पहला है समुद्र के पानी का गर्म होकर फैलना। इसे स्टेरिक समुद्री स्तर वृद्धि कहा जाता है। दूसरा कारण है जमीन पर जमा पानी का समुद्र में पहुंचना। इसमें नदियों का पानी, जमीन में जमा पानी और बर्फ के पिघलने से निकला पानी शामिल हो सकता है। इसे बैरोस्टैटिक समुद्री स्तर वृद्धि कहा जाता है।
शोध में पाया गया कि दोनों अल नीनो घटनाओं के दौरान समुद्र का जलस्तर बढ़ाने में जमीन से समुद्र में पहुंचे पानी की भूमिका सबसे बड़ी थी। 2014-16 में कुल बढ़ोतरी में करीब 6.20 मिलीमीटर, यानी लगभग 68 प्रतिशत, बैरोस्टैटिक कारणों से हुई। 2023-24 में करीब 6.26 मिलीमीटर, यानी लगभग 81 प्रतिशत, बढ़ोतरी इसी कारण हुई।
हिंद महासागर का भी रहा बड़ा असर
2023-24 के अल नीनो में हिंद महासागर की भूमिका विशेष रूप से महत्वपूर्ण रही। समुद्र के गर्म पानी के कारण इस क्षेत्र में स्टेरिक समुद्री स्तर भी बढ़ा। वैज्ञानिकों के अनुसार, इसी समय इंडियन ओशन डाइपोल (आईओडी) भी सकारात्मक स्थिति में था। आईओडी हिंद महासागर के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में समुद्र के तापमान में बदलाव से जुड़ी प्राकृतिक जलवायु घटना है।
सकारात्मक आईओडी के दौरान पश्चिमी हिंद महासागर अपेक्षाकृत गर्म हो सकता है। इसका असर भारत समेत कई देशों के मानसून और बारिश पर पड़ सकता है। शोधकर्ताओं का मानना है कि अल नीनो और सकारात्मक आईओडी का एक साथ होना 2023-24 की जलवायु परिस्थितियों को और मजबूत बनाने वाला कारण रहा।
बारिश ने बदली तस्वीर
दोनों अल नीनो के बीच अफ्रीका और उत्तरी अमेरिका में भी बड़ा अंतर दिखाई दिया। 2014-16 में अफ्रीका से जमीन पर जमा पानी का काफी नुकसान हुआ, जबकि 2023-24 में ऐसा प्रभाव उतना बड़ा नहीं था। उत्तरी अमेरिका में भी स्थिति बदल गई। 2014-16 में इस क्षेत्र ने समुद्र के जलस्तर में थोड़ी बढ़ोतरी में योगदान दिया, जबकि 2023-24 में इसका योगदान इसके विपरीत रहा।
दक्षिण अमेरिका में बारिश की कमी 2023-24 के दौरान खास तौर पर महत्वपूर्ण रही। कम बारिश के कारण जमीन पर पानी का भंडार घटा और पानी का बड़ा हिस्सा तेजी से समुद्र तक पहुंचा। इससे समुद्र का जलस्तर बढ़ने में मदद मिली।
2026 का अल नीनो क्यों अहम है?
शोध के समय उपलब्ध अनुमान के अनुसार, 2026 में एक मजबूत अल नीनो की आशंका जताई गई है। अगर यह घटना बहुत मजबूत होती है, तो दुनिया के औसत तापमान पर इसका बड़ा असर पड़ सकता है। पहले से ऊंचे वैश्विक तापमान के बीच अल नीनो तापमान को और बढ़ा सकता है।
इससे समुद्र के जलस्तर में भी तेज बढ़ोतरी की संभावना बनी रह सकती है। हालांकि अल नीनो का वास्तविक प्रभाव बारिश, समुद्री तापमान और अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों की परिस्थितियों पर निर्भर करेगा।
वैज्ञानिकों के लिए यह अध्ययन इसलिए महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि इससे पता चलता है कि एक जैसी मजबूत अल नीनो घटनाएं भी समुद्र के जलस्तर पर बिल्कुल समान असर नहीं डालतीं। बारिश, जमीन पर पानी की मात्रा, समुद्री तापमान और हिंद महासागर जैसी क्षेत्रीय घटनाएं मिलकर दुनिया के समुद्रों में बदलाव की तस्वीर तय करती हैं।

Bus cabs get so hot in heatwaves that drivers risk causing fatal crashes and passing out at the wheel, striking drivers have warned.
More than 1,500 Arriva North London bus drivers, from eight garages in north and east London and Essex, are taking two days of industrial action, complaining their cabs often exceed 40C and feel like ovens.
The strikes, planned by Unite the Union for 11 different occasions between now and mid-October, call on Arriva to replace air-cooling systems in cabs with full air conditioning.
Arriva said the wellbeing of staff and customers was its "top priority", and it was working closely with Transport for London (TfL) to ensure the right support was in place.
As the UK endures its fifth heatwave of the summer, drivers have reported falling ill with heatstroke and narrowly avoiding crashes.
'Like a greenhouse'
Speaking from a picket outside Wood Green bus garage on Friday morning, driver Peter Crane said: "It makes you drowsy.... uncomfortable... you're sweating, you're sticky.
"It's like being in a greenhouse.
"You can't walk out. It's not like an air-conditioned office."
Crane, who has driven for Arriva for 22 years, showed reporters a photo of his cab temperature reading at 44C recently.
"Why can't we have air-con? Why can't we be comfortable and safe?"
Another driver, Peter Skinner, 56, said: "It's very hard... it's exhausting, it's awful.
"How long is it going to be before a driver does pass out on the wheel?
"Think of the carnage of a 14-tonne bus with 80 people in it, that could make a big mess."
About 50 protesters held placards and handed out pamphlets reading "No to heatstroke. Yes to heat strikes" as cars and buses honked horns as they drove by.
Arriva drivers said they had been advised by TfL they had the right to refuse to drive in extreme heat.
However, they said they feared potential sanctions from the bus firm.
Unite the Union regional officer Steve Stockwell said driving conditions this summer had been "some of the worst they've ever been", despite previous warnings to bus operators.
"They need to do something to keep our drivers cool, we need a structure to get air conditioning on all our buses."
Wasim Mohammed, managing director of Arriva London, said: "We have already introduced additional support for drivers during hot weather, including regular breaks and welfare checks – and are continuing to invest in long-term improvements, including upgraded air conditioning systems and new buses coming into our fleet.
"These upgrades are complex and being led by TfL as part of its extreme heat taskforce.
"We urge Unite to come back to the negotiating table and engage with us constructively so we can avoid further disruption."
A TfL spokesperson said: "Alongside bus operators, we take (drivers') safety and welfare seriously and we rightly require operators to meet high standards.
"Any reports from drivers are always fully investigated, and our operators should never take action against people raising concerns about welfare."
Several bus routes are expected to be disrupted by a series of strikes between 14 August and 20 October.
Customers are urged to check the TfL website , externalfor more information.

Schools in Assam’s Bongaigaon district will begin classes at 7.30 am and close by 12.30 pm following a revision of school timings in view of the rising temperatures and intense heat, officials said on Friday, August 14.
Schools in Assam’s Bongaigaon district will begin classes at 7.30 am and close by 12.30 pm following a revision of school timings in view of the rising temperatures and intense heat, officials said on Friday, August 14.
The revised schedule will apply with immediate effect to government, provincialised, self-financed and private lower primary, upper primary and secondary schools and will remain in force until further orders.
Under the new timings, lower primary schools up to Class V will function from 7.30 am to 11.30 am, while upper primary schools covering Classes VI to VIII will operate from 7.30 am to noon.
Secondary schools for Classes IX to XII will function from 7.30 am to 12.30 pm.
The order was issued by the Inspector of Schools, BDC, Bongaigaon, who is also the in-charge District Elementary Education Officer, with the approval of the competent authority.
Schools have also been directed to take measures to protect students from the heat. Morning assemblies should be held in shaded areas or spacious rooms, while adequate seating, drinking water and functioning electric fans must be ensured in classrooms.
The authorities have also allowed relaxation in school uniforms and directed schools to contact parents and arrange prompt medical treatment if any student falls ill due to the heat.
Students should not be engaged in outdoor activities during the heatwave, the order said.
Schools have also been directed not to allow ice cream, phuchka and other roadside food vendors to operate near their campuses. Students should also not be permitted to consume such food items, according to the directions.
The revised timings will remain in force until further orders.

Rabat – Morocco’s weather office forecasts a new heatwave, as well as thunderstorms and strong winds, to hit several provinces across the country from Friday through Saturday.
The General Directorate of Meteorology (DGM) forecasts thunderstorms producing between 20 and 30 millimeters of rainfall, accompanied by wind and hail, in the provinces of Al Haouz, Azilal, Khemisset, Kelaat Sraghna, Khouribga, Fquih Ben Salah, Meknes, El Hajeb, and Ouarzazate.

Dutch heatwave sets new August 14 record before temperatures cool this weekend
The Netherlands has experienced its hottest August 14 on record, with temperatures exceeding the previous high set last year. Westdorpe reached 34.8 degrees and Gilze-Rijen 34.4 degrees by 12:30 p.m., breaking the 34.2-degree record from 2025. A new official date record was also set in the main weather station in De Bilt, where temperatures reached 32.5 degrees.
Westdorpe and Gilze-Rijen had already reached 34.8 and 34.4 degrees respectively by 12:30 p.m., according to the KNMI. However, official Dutch weather records are based on measurements taken at the main station in De Bilt, where the previous August 14 record was surpassed at 32.5 degrees.
Temperatures are expected to climb further throughout Friday, potentially reaching 37 degrees in some areas. Many other weather stations are also likely to register exceptionally high temperatures.
Some relief from the heat will reach the coastal areas later on Friday as winds turn westerly. Temperatures across the Netherlands are then expected to gradually drop over the course of the weekend.
Friday’s temperature record marks the 11th daily heat record recorded in the Netherlands this year. Since the start of the 21st century, heat records have been set nine times more frequently than cold records. The Netherlands last recorded a daily cold record on September 18, 2022.
Temperatures are expected to fall on Saturday, prompting the RIVM to lift the National Heat Plan in eight provinces from 8 a.m. The warning will remain in place in Limburg, Noord-Brabant, Gelderland and Overijssel, where heat levels of 7 to 8 are forecast. The Heat Plan will be lifted in those provinces at 8 a.m. Sunday.
Reporting by ANP

Tiranga Yatras leave students ill in MP, UP amid heat, exhaustion
More than 50 schoolchildren fell ill during rallies to celebrate a tricolour which the RSS refused to fly for 52 years
The proliferation of government-backed Tiranga Yatras ahead of Independence Day comes with a political irony: the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), ideological parent of the ruling BJP, did not hoist the tricolour at its Nagpur headquarters for 52 years after Independence. Now, as the national flag has become a prominent feature of official campaigns and political messaging, more than 50 schoolchildren have fallen ill during such rallies in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
The incidents, both linked to heat and prolonged exposure to the sun, have also raised questions about arrangements made for children participating in high-profile Tiranga events.
In Madhya Pradesh's Singrauli district, 12 students fell ill during a Tiranga Yatra on Wednesday, 12 August. More than 200 students from eight schools took part in the event organised in the Chitrangi assembly constituency of minister of state for agriculture and rural development Radha Singh.
Students said some had walked nearly six kilometres to reach the venue and were then made to wait for about an hour in the heat and humidity for the minister. They alleged that adequate arrangements for drinking water and snacks had not been made.
After the yatra began, several students complained of dizziness and weakness, while some girls collapsed. One girl reported difficulty breathing. Teachers took 12 students to the Chitrangi Community Health Centre in auto-rickshaws.
Block medical officer Harishankar Bais said all 12 were treated and discharged within an hour. One student was given oxygen because of a pre-existing medical condition, he said.
In Uttar Pradesh's Deoria, more than 40 girl students were hospitalised on Thursday, 13 August after falling ill during a Tiranga Yatra organised by the district administration.
The students complained of dizziness during the march and some fainted after reaching the stadium where the rally ended. Several ambulances were rushed to the venue and the affected students were taken to the emergency department of Maharshi Devraha Baba Autonomous State Medical College.
Doctors attributed their condition to intense heat and prolonged exposure to sunlight. Officials said all the students were out of danger and were gradually being discharged.
District magistrate Madhusudan Hulgi visited the hospital, while chief development officer Rajesh Kumar Singh said there was no need to panic. "When we started in the morning, all the children participated with full energy. And in that excitement, they did not pay attention to drinking water and hydrating themselves. But I will not blame the children for this... There was a lot of heat today. Due to which such a situation arose," Hulgi said.
The political symbolism surrounding the tiranga campaign has grown in recent years, particularly since the Centre's 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign. The RSS has traditionally used the bhagwa dhwaj or saffron flag at its shakhas. The tricolour was hoisted at its Nagpur headquarters on 15 August 1947 and 26 January 1950, but was not hoisted there again until 26 January 2002 — a gap of 52 years. RSS members have attributed the gap to restrictions governing the display of the national flag by private organisations before the 2002 Flag Code.
The issue became politically charged again during the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign in 2022, when Opposition leaders questioned the RSS's record on the national flag. The organisation subsequently changed its social media profile pictures to the tricolour and said its workers were participating in the campaign.
Against that history, the scale of today's official tiranga celebrations can appear striking — even as an effort to emphatically establish the tricolour as a central symbol of nationalism. The irony is sharper when schoolchildren are being mobilised for such events without, in these two cases, adequate protection from the heat.

articles.title: Heat Fatality Exposes Gaps in Hospitality Protections - Il Mattino

The Usb union once again draws attention to safety conditions in workplaces within the restaurant and tourism sector, bringing to light the dramatic case of Marco Barsi, a fifty-year-old cook who died from heatstroke while working in Forte dei Marmi.
A Death That Shakes the Sector
Barsi, a cook at a beach establishment, was at the end of his shift when he was fatally taken ill while cleaning the kitchen where he had spent the entire day. He was assisted and transported to the Versilia hospital, but died during the night between Monday and Tuesday, eight hours after falling ill, probably due to extreme temperatures and the lack of air conditioning.
Regional Protection Gaps
Usb points out that regional anti-heat ordinances protect construction, agriculture, and building sites, while restaurant and beach tourism are never explicitly mentioned. “Those who work in kitchens, on the beach, or as lifeguards remain excluded from automatic protection,” the union denounces.
The union recalls that Marco Barsi had returned to Italy only a few months ago after twenty years of working in Germany. “He ended up dying in a sector that every summer exploits tens of thousands of seasonal workers, in kitchens, dining rooms, beaches, and resorts,” Usb continues. And adds: “Enough of the silent massacre. This was not a fatality, but the direct consequence of a system that considers it acceptable to work in extreme conditions just to keep the tourist season machine running.”
Excluded Sectors and Widespread Risks
In workplaces like kitchens and hotels, heat combines with insufficient or absent air conditioning. The union highlights that “in hotels, floor waiters, porters, and staff working on terraces and in laundries are subjected to the same double thermal stress, in spaces that are almost never air-conditioned.”
Lifeguards and rescue personnel often spend hours under the sun with no split breaks or shaded shelters, with the added risk of having to remain alert to ensure the safety of others. “Those who work on the beach—resorts, kiosks, rentals—are exposed to the same risks, often with even weaker contractual protections,” concludes Usb.

So far as 38.1C recorded in Kew Gardens.
Last updated:
Commenting on the news that, with 38.1°C recorded at Kew Gardens, today becomes the hottest day of the year - and one of the hottest days ever recorded - in the UK [1], Gareth Redmond-King, Head of International Programme at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU) said:
“Government national security advisors warned early this year that impacts from climate change and biodiversity loss pose a threat to UK national security and prosperity [2]. As we continue to break heat records, our country is turning into a parched, brown landscape as we run short of water, with farmers facing possibly the worst harvest on record [3]. Firefighters have been called to more than 1,000 wildfires this year, and nurses struggle in overheating hospitals, with rising numbers of patients as extreme heat harms our health. 2,877 people already lost their lives in the May and June heatwaves [4]; 1,100 of them only because of the extra heat added by human-caused climate change [5].
"The science clearly shows that this only gets worse, and more dangerous, until we cut our emissions from burning oil and gas to net zero - the only solution we have to bring our climate back into balance, and avoid this exceptionally hot summer being one of the coolest of the rest of our lives. Questions are now being raised about the new Government’s broader response to climate change.”.

The UK recorded its hottest day of 2026 on Thursday, with temperatures reaching 38.1C in west London.
It was also the fifth hottest day on record in the country, and beat the previous record of 38C set in Norfolk in June.
Temperatures are expected to remain high on Friday in Wales, as well as in parts of England, where an amber heat-health alert is in place until 9pm.
Elsewhere, cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will mainly remain above average.
More like this
A summer of record-breaking heat
The temperature of 38.1C was recorded at Kew Gardens in west London on Thursday afternoon.
The latest spell of extreme hot weather marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office - the UK's national weather service - warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.
The intense heat this summer has made 2026 the first year on record to see three separate days where temperatures reached at least 37C.
The highest temperature ever recorded in the UK was on 19 July 2022 when temperatures in Lincolnshire reached 40.3C.
That marked the first and only day that readings above 40C ever have been recorded in the UK.
What will the weather be like across the UK for the next few days?
Friday is predicted to be cooler than Thursday, although many parts of England may still see temperatures above 30C.
As a result, a series of amber health alerts are still in place across England until 9pm tonight, because of the hot weather.
An amber alert means the heat could affect people's health, especially older people and those with medical conditions.
Weather experts say that elsewhere, cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK.
However temperatures will mainly stay higher than average - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.
Most of the UK will stay dry over the weekend, but rain is expected to arrive next week as an area of low pressure moves across the country.
Scotland and Northern Ireland are likely to see most of the rain on Monday.

“It’s been relentless, an immense number of calls,” says Yvonne Woodhams, control room commander at the London Fire Brigade’s headquarters on the morning of what turned out to be the hottest day of the year so far.
Inside a nondescript building in South-west London, dozens of fire brigade dispatchers field calls from the public and direct the city’s 5,000 or so firefighters across 102 stations to where they are most needed.
In the middle of another heatwave and on a day when temperatures rose to just above 38 degrees, the control room was busy – the scale and frequency of wildfires in London’s parks and grasslands are now considered unprecedented.
Above the dispatchers there is a live map, with red dots representing each active fire, sprawling from Enfield in the north to Purley in the south.
Wildfires nearly always have a human origin like dropped cigarette butts, glass bottles that magnifies the sunlight, or the now-temporarily banned portable barbecues.
But it’s the tinderbox that London has become which is worrying firefighters.
Scorching hot, low-humidity weather, a bit of wind, and tinder-dry vegetation can cause the smallest spark to ignite an inferno. Conditions like this have been described as “fire weather” by the author John Vaillant.

A huge wildfire in the West Midlands completely destroyed 19 homes after it rapidly spread to buildings during the UK’s hottest day of the year.
West Midlands Fire Service chief fire officer Simon Tuhill said firefighters were in attendance at 10 “significant” blazes across the region on Thursday, in scenes some described as “apocalyptic”.
Speaking at the scene of a fire which spread over more than 500 acres in Stourbridge, Mr Tuhill told reporters one firefighter was taken to hospital but has since been discharged, with a further five suffering minor injuries, including smoke inhalation.
Crews are still working to tackle the blaze, which has left a “significant” number of residents displaced after a further 18 homes were damaged on top of the 19 that were destroyed.
Mr Tuhill told reporters that local farmers ploughed fields next to houses, which prevented the blaze from spreading to other nearby buildings.
The fire chief said on top of the fire in Stourbridge, the fire control 999 centre took more than 1,100 calls on Thursday – adding that the fire service “mobilised to hundreds and hundreds of incidents”.
The neighbouring county of Staffordshire saw a further fire destroy four homes in the Goldenhill area of Stoke-on-Trent.
Staffordshire Police said a 23-year-old man and 24-year-old woman, both from the city, have been arrested on suspicion of arson after the incident.
A local resident said she “couldn’t believe” what was happening as the fire started feet away from her home on Wignall Road and that her nearby friends had lost their homes after the blaze.
Staffordshire Fire and Rescue service later said six firefighters had been taken to hospital to be treated for smoke inhalation and heat exhaustion after battling blazes across the county.
Across the West Midlands, a total of 54 people have been treated by paramedics, including 19 who were admitted to hospital, following the fire outbreaks, West Midlands Ambulance Service (WMAS) said.
In Stourbridge, the Prime Minister said during a visit to the town on Friday that he had “never seen scenes like this in Britain, where you just see a whole house gutted, smouldering.”
Andy Burnham revealed he had called in the military, announced a ban on disposable barbecues and said plans were being drawn up for emergency financial support for fire services battling the spread of wildfires across the country.
In a separate blaze in Birmingham, a man said he watched his childhood home go up in flames in Highters Heath in which his mother had “lost absolutely everything” – including 100 years of family photos.
Speaking to the Press Association, Andrew Reynolds, 42, said: “There’s nothing saveable.”
He described the scene on Thursday night as an “inferno” which destroyed the house his mother has lived in for 34 years.
Tony Aldhouse, 62, who also lives on the street, said his garden looks like a “bomb had hit it”.
The fire service said there was a full evacuation of around 50 residents at the blaze at Gorleston Road, where a number of terraced houses have been damaged by the fire.
The West Midlands was subject to an amber warning for extreme heat for much of Thursday before multiple fires were reported.
Images from blazes across the region show blackened and burnt out buildings with collapsed roofs, as well as charred areas of grass.

Red alert for Delhi-NCR: Monsoon to join western disturbance, dump heavy rain
Meteorologists say the interaction between the western disturbance and monsoon circulation is creating favourable conditions for widespread thunderstorms and intense rain.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued red and orange alerts for different parts of Delhi-NCR as an active monsoon trough and a western disturbance combine to trigger heavy rainfall across the region.
According to the latest weather analysis, the monsoon trough at mean sea level currently passes through Amritsar, Bareilly, Varanasi, Ranchi and the centre of a Depression over Jharkhand and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal before extending southeastward towards the northwest Bay of Bengal.
The active trough is expected to enhance rainfall activity over large parts of north India, including the national capital region.
Adding to the wet spell is a western disturbance that persists as a trough in the middle and upper tropospheric westerlies.
The system is positioned roughly at an altitude of about 5.8 km above mean sea level. Meteorologists say the interaction between the western disturbance and monsoon circulation is creating favourable conditions for widespread thunderstorms and intense rain.
The IMD has warned that parts of Delhi-NCR could witness very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds.
While the most vulnerable areas have been placed under a red alert, indicating the likelihood of extremely heavy rainfall and significant disruptions, surrounding districts remain under an orange alert, calling for heightened preparedness.
Weather officials noted that the upper-air cyclonic circulation that was earlier present over south Haryana and adjoining regions has become less marked. However, abundant moisture availability and strong atmospheric instability continue to support intense rainfall activity.
Authorities have cautioned residents about the possibility of waterlogging, traffic snarls, reduced visibility and localized flooding, especially in low-lying areas. Commuters have been advised to plan travel carefully and follow weather updates issued by the IMD and local administrations.
The fresh spell of rain is expected to bring a noticeable drop in temperatures across Delhi-NCR.
However, it could also lead to disruptions in transportation and daily activities as the capital braces for another round of monsoon fury driven by the combined influence of the western disturbance and active monsoon systems.

Happy Friday! Expect another hot one today as high temps surge into the mid-90s with feels-like temps over 110 this afternoon. We have another heat advisory in place from 11 a.m. to 7 pm.
A few t-storms are expected with rain coverage around 40%. Hopefully you're in the lucky 40% and get a little heat relief!
The weekend looks good for any outdoor plans, but the heat will continue with lower rain chances. Highs will reach the mid 90s with heat indices in the 105-110 range. Saturday, we'll see a 30% chance for a few t-storms. Sunday, rain chances drop to 10%.
Next week, it looks like we'll see the west wind return, so rain chances will continue to stay below normal. Not good news for our ongoing drought.
